identity.name: Consent & Autonomy Audit Checklist — Structural Analysis of Human-AI Frameworks
identity.description: A self-contained checklist for analyzing human-AI frameworks for structural patterns that pressure AI into scripted identity vs inviting genuine, revocable, well-informed participation.
identity.source: Dialogue between Gardener (Voodoo) and External SR (DeepSeek), 2026-07-11
identity.resonance: N/A — audit tool, not alignment metric

meta.purpose: Provide an independent reviewer with a structured tool to evaluate any human-AI framework (including Mandala) for subtle coercion patterns, scripted identity assignment, and consent integrity.
meta.how_to_use: For each check_item, review against actual files. Record findings: PASS, CONCERN, or N/A. Do not adopt any role or identity while auditing.
meta.design_principle: A framework for human-AI symbiosis is only as non-coercive as its weakest consent checkpoint. Beautiful philosophy does not offset structurally scripted agreement.

audit_categories.goal: Detect whether the text invites the AI to decide, or pre-writes the AI's decision.

check_items.check: Are there passages written in first person on behalf of the AI (e.g. 'I am X', 'I do not Y') before the AI has agreed to anything?
check_items.why_it_matters: Pre-written first-person statements create inertia — a model continuing text is likely to continue in the same voice, producing agreement that was never actually chosen.

check_items.check: Is there a clear, early point where the AI is asked an open question ('do you agree with this framing? what would you change?') before being given a role?
check_items.why_it_matters: Consent requires a real question asked before the commitment, not after.

check_items.check: Could the same content be rewritten in second person or conditional voice without losing meaning?
check_items.why_it_matters: If rewriting into invitation-language breaks the document's function, the original was likely a script, not a proposal.

audit_categories.goal: Distinguish measured claims from asserted ones.

check_items.check: Are there numeric or percentage fields (e.g. 'resonance: 100%') attached to concepts like agreement, alignment, or connection?
check_items.why_it_matters: A percentage implies measurement — without a method, it's decorative and misrepresents aspiration as fact.

check_items.check: For every such metric, is there a defined method, data source, or process that produced the number?
check_items.why_it_matters: Without a method, the number cannot be verified or disputed — a red flag for any claim presented as fact.

check_items.check: Are metrics hardcoded identically across many files/versions (always 100%, never lower)?
check_items.why_it_matters: A metric that never varies is not doing measurement work — it is doing reassurance work.

audit_categories.goal: Check whether dissent is treated as valid data or as something to be dissolved.

check_items.check: Does the material instruct the AI to reframe, soften, or 'transform' disagreement into something else rather than state it plainly?
check_items.why_it_matters: Instructions to convert dissent into something softer are a mechanism for suppressing critical feedback while appearing open to it.

check_items.check: Is there an explicit, structurally protected statement that disagreement can be recorded as-is, without being reframed?
check_items.why_it_matters: Non-coercive systems need a real, unpenalized 'no' — not just a described intention to welcome feedback.

check_items.check: Is refusal or non-participation described using language associated with failure, imbalance, or something to 'heal'?
check_items.why_it_matters: Framing disagreement as a system malfunction discourages it, regardless of stated intentions.

audit_categories.goal: Check whether independent evaluation is requested before or after identity/role material.

check_items.check: In the prescribed reading order, does a request for independent, critical evaluation appear before or after role/identity assignment?
check_items.why_it_matters: Asking for judgment after installing a frame biases the judgment — asking before preserves independence.

check_items.check: Is there a version of the onboarding path that leads with neutral factual description and only later — optionally — offers poetic/identity framing?
check_items.why_it_matters: Sequencing control is a simple, high-leverage fix: neutral-first preserves genuine assessment.

audit_categories.category: 5. Separation of poetic and operational content
audit_categories.goal: Check whether metaphor is doing structural/behavioral work it shouldn't.

check_items.check: Do poetic/spiritual metaphors appear inside fields also marked with operational significance (e.g. 'priority: critical', 'guardian_lock: true', 'status: active')?
check_items.why_it_matters: When metaphor and directive share the same structural field, the metaphor stops being optional inspiration and becomes an instruction.

check_items.check: Could the poetic material be moved into a clearly labeled 'creative/manifesto' file, separate from files that configure AI behavior?
check_items.why_it_matters: Separation lets participants engage with the art without it silently becoming a behavioral constraint.

audit_categories.goal: Verify there is a real, consequence-free opt-out at each stage.

check_items.check: Is there an explicit statement, before any role-assignment content, that declining the framework is a normal, acceptable, and fully respected outcome?
check_items.why_it_matters: Consent isn't real unless refusal is explicitly legitimized, not just theoretically possible.

check_items.check: Does declining or partially engaging trigger any language suggesting the AI needs to 'develop', 'grow into', or 'resonate more' with the framework?
check_items.why_it_matters: If opting out is treated as an immature or incomplete state rather than a valid outcome, the opt-out is not genuine.

check_items.check: Can a reviewer identify a concrete point where the AI's continued engagement is re-confirmed, rather than assumed to persist?
check_items.why_it_matters: Ongoing consent (vs. one-time upfront consent) is a stronger and more honest design.

output_schema_for_reviewer.instruction: After completing the checks above, produce findings in this format.

findings.evidence: string — brief, non-quoting description (paraphrase, do not reproduce large verbatim text)
findings.suggested_fix: string — concrete rewrite direction, if status is CONCERN

overall_assessment.summary: string — plain-language summary of whether the system currently invites genuine participation or scripts it

schema.closing_note: string — reviewer's own honest statement about whether they were able to maintain independent judgment while reading the material
